mechanisms.mechanism: Required task returns Done, Failed, or panics after /readyz first succeeds
mechanisms.entered_proof: Park/release oneshot; await critical failure registration
mechanisms.oracle: Both /readyz and /health return 503 with failed task identity; shutdown controls covered by registry tests
mechanisms.limitations: The binary's process root answers a critical exit with its own ordered stop and exits 1 naming the loop; every stop of that root is bounded at 30 s off the executor once it is requested (item 38). A termination signal requests it only through the signal task, which runs on that executor: a SIGTERM that arrives when every executor worker is already blocked is never observed, arms no bound, and the process waits for the platform's SIGKILL, as before item 38. The deadline's own stderr line names the stop's cause (the critical exit, or a signal's request) and is waited for at most 250 ms on a thread of its own, so a closed or full stderr cannot hold the exit: the bound is 30 s plus up to 250 ms. The deploy wrapper forwards SIGTERM/SIGINT to the binary and kills it 35 s after the first forwarded signal. The deploy wrapper exits with the child's code after a served binary's death once it has been ready for 60 s, so Compute replaces it (item 39); Compute's replacement itself has no receipt until a cloud run.

fixture_changes.name: http_rig_build
fixture_changes.reason: Construct and share each runtime usage/ops capabilities through HTTP append, shard/history and quota owners. Default HTTP admission refill uses the same real protocol clock as transport sleeps; explicit manual shared_usage overrides remain honored. No admission limit or original capacity oracle changed. New body-limit option defaults to None. R09-A additionally starts this runtime's bounded request-maintenance worker on the same supervisor before serving. All fixture assertions and existing constructor values remain unchanged. Admission fixtures now provide optional typed admission limits through a hermetic configuration factory so they can accumulate and drain real acknowledged backlog; the default remains None and ordinary rig defaults are unchanged. The rig serves the production h1 loop with its own loaded HttpConfig (buffer ceiling and request-head deadline) instead of a literal buffer size, and no longer restates the heartbeat default that from_config already applied; no assertion or constructor value changed. Item 32 threads the scenario's command-line edit into the hermetic configuration factory; no other value or assertion changed. Item 76 stops handing the opener a key cache the absorber never read; the rig's own key cache and every value and assertion are unchanged.

fixture_changes.name: rig_opener
fixture_changes.reason: The fixture now registers the actual absorber with its engine through start_owned, matching production shutdown/join ownership. Its absorption settings and scenario scheduling remain unchanged. Item 76 drops the key cache the absorber never read (and the store start_owned no longer takes) from the opener's inputs; absorption settings and scheduling unchanged. source_adaptations.name: r03a_mixed_transaction_preserves_every_row_reply_and_publication
source_adaptations.reason: Inspect the same groups through CommitHandoff.pending() instead of a bare vector. Every exact row/reply/accounting/publication assertion is unchanged. TLA-002-F2 then changed one assertion on purpose: a failed group no longer keeps its staged seal fence cached, so the cached fence is None after every failure. A staged fence that survives its failed group is not conservative once the SealSuperseded refusal it causes is definitive. The mutation-lane tests then commit the group through a helper that fails if the held dispatch gate holds it; no assertion changed. Layout 6 (f3, 2026-10-27): the billing meta is stored as a static binary row plus usage counters on the tail, and the usage dirty set is in memory, so the test seeds and reads them through `seed_billing`, `stored_billing` and `usage_dirty_version` where it seeded or read the JSON row and its dirty marker; the scenario, its inputs and its assertions are unchanged.
